CONTRACT SURFACE the laws pin — src/lease.ts: export const HOSTED_LEASE_MS = 60 * 60 * 1000; export const DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES = { renew: '/rest/v1/rpc/coltrane_drain_renew', release: '/rest/v1/rpc/coltrane_drain_release' }; renew: POST ${COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL}${DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES.renew} body {p_gig_id} ONLY, Bearer drain key (the route fills p_token), X-Coltrane-Instance (the route fills p_instance); 200 -> new lease_until; 403 / 42501 -> lease lost; release: POST ${COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL}${DRAIN_LEASE_ROUTES.release} body {p_gig_id, p_reason, p_terminal} ONLY, instance in X-Coltrane-Instance -> boolean; WorkOnceDeps.scheduleHeartbeat: (intervalMs: number, beat: () => Promise<unknown>) => () => void; default arms an unref'd setInterval; interval = HOSTED_LEASE_MS / 3; WorkOnceResult.acknowledged: boolean on a claimed result: true iff the store acknowledged the terminal header; terminal header attempts: 3; header status: 'running' is a new GigHeaderRecord status, sent awaited before the first chair with the run's genome_hash; manifest.cold_run_reason: string on a header written by a run that went cold because a resume was refused. ROUND 2: output drains are acknowledged (3 attempts) before the completed header; a 'running' header refused with 23514 or 403/42501 aborts the run with no terminal write. ROUND 3 (branch work/gig-runs-once-r3): G1 the heartbeat stays armed until the terminal header is acknowledged or exhausted; G2 no release after the outcome is decided when the terminal header is unacknowledged; REFUND a non-terminal release only before the first chair invocation; Q6 the drain deadline ends a gig aborted/timeout (WorkOnceResult status 'aborted', aborted:{reason:'timeout'}, header status 'aborted', no gig_fail); G4 (terminal rows only; founder ruling, Eugene: "what's closed is closed. can refer to the sealed outputs on input if needed but reopening doesn't smell right."): the successful resume path at gig_dispatch(resume_gig_id) / `coltrane dispatch --resume` runs today under the OLD id (gigId = resumeArg ?? randomUUID()), which the store's terminal guard answers with 23514; a resume of a failed/aborted gig must dispatch a NEW gig carrying resumes:<old id>, take the old seals as inputs by reference (content_sha in input_shas, never re-sealed), and write nothing under the old id. The refused-resume case is covered by tests/resume_reuse_dispatch.test.ts:164. A parked → approved → re-claimed gig is not terminal and keeps its id (E6b records a cold run there). G4 hosted: the store's claim carries resumes:<old id|null>; workOnce runs under the claim's own id, takes the closed gig's drained seals (coltrane_mcp_gig_outputs for the old id) as inputs by reference, invokes no chair already sealed there, and writes nothing under the old id. The gig_dispatch resume law covers both terminal endings, failed and aborted. ROUND 4 (branch work/gig-runs-once-r4, on the implementation at 16b00dc): WorkOnceResult.status vocabulary is complete | failed | awaiting_approval | aborted | abandoned — `abandoned` = the lease was lost (a refused renew, or a start header refused with 23514 / 403-42501): the worker writes nothing terminal, no gig_fail, no release, and acknowledged:false; it is NOT a failure of the gig and NOT an outcome the store should record from this worker. L1 a late answer after a lost lease is never sealed; E7c a stale holder of a requeued local row is refused; Q6r the aborted header carries manifest.abort_reason = "timeout" as a field; L4 with a store present (ServerDeps.gigStatus → coltrane_mcp_gig_status) the store decides whether a gig is closed for G4. (G4b/G4h cite their laws at 5993cff on work/gig-runs-once-r3; they arrive on this line with the implementer's merge of 4ed5ef4.) ROUND 5 (on 30183e1): R5.1 a resumed gig re-claimed on a fresh box rebuilds from the closed gig's seals AND its own; R5.2 a store that throws or never answers (30 s) refuses the resume — never a checkpoint fallback; R5.3 the closed set is failed|aborted|completed|cancelled, the open set running|queued|awaiting_approval; R5.4 rpcGigStatus (coltrane_mcp_gig_status → status) drives the decision. OBLIGATION OUTSIDE THIS REPO: the HOST (eir-labs/coltrane-ui) must wire ServerDeps.gigStatus = rpcGigStatus(...) the way it wires queueGig — until it does, no hosted door has a store to ask and the checkpoint decides. This is a coltrane-ui follow-up after #554 publishes. ROUND 6 (RED at 2d4e7ab): the HOSTED gig_dispatch branch (createToolSurface → callSurfaceTool, deps.queueGig) must make the same closed-gig decision as the local door: H1 a closed gig's resume queues resumes:<old id> (never resume_gig_id); H2 an open gig's resume is refused (in-place resume is gig_approve's job); H3 a store that throws, never answers (30 s) or is not wired refuses, nothing queued; H4 queueGig receives ONLY the host contract (standard_slug, mode, input, org_slug, acting_for, venue, resumes — what postgrestQueueGig/rpcQueueGig read, plus resumes) and every other advertised gig_dispatch argument (chart_slug, repo_url, depth, effort, max_context_tokens, budget, reuse, approvals, approved_by, wait:true) is refused BY NAME. Budget carriage (a store column) and the coltrane-ui adapter's mapping of `resumes` are the coltrane-ui follow-up. ROUND 6b (review 5326196799 at 2d4e7ab): the fixture now enforces the live store's gig-token scope (status: own gig; outputs: own + the gig the row resumes; else 403/42501) and the drain service's real refusal shape ({error}, no code; 401/403/400 by message) — G4h and R5.1 are therefore RED AT HEAD, as found live. D1 a resuming gig never re-pays for the closed gig's seals under the real scope (fix: the store widens the resume exception to gig_status, or the engine reads the closed gig's genome hash from somewhere its token may read, e.g. the claim); D2 player mode's run timeout stays under its 30-minute lease (the player path has no renew RPC, so it is the timeout, not a heartbeat); D3 ANY non-2xx on the start header (400 without a code, 403, a persistent 503) stops the run before the first chair; S2–S4 book the review's surviving plants. Not booked (review finding 5, low): output-drain state is per process; the CLI is one gig per process. D1 RESOLVED BY THE STORE (conductor): the fixture now mirrors the coltrane-ui follow-up scope (status + outputs readable for exactly the resumed gig), under which G4h, R5.1 and D1 pass at 2d4e7ab; they stay dependent on that follow-up deploying before #554's hosted resume is live. D3-503 requires E2's retries (3 attempts) on the start header before the run stops. Q1/Q2: the engine's queue clients (postgrestQueueGig, rpcQueueGig) never drop resumes/budget_micro_usd — send (p_resumes, p_budget_micro_usd) or refuse by name; absent → no key. FINDING: at coltrane-ui work/host-carries-the-gig neither coltrane_gig_dispatch nor coltrane_mcp_dispatch accepts those parameters (no migration touches their signatures; the host's dispatch is app-side, src/lib/dispatch.ts, taking resumes / budget_micro_usd verbatim), so today only the REFUSE branch of Q1 is deployable; sending the p_ keys needs a store migration first (PostgREST resolves by exact argument names — the 0.24.12 p_venue outage). A1: a drain key without COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL refuses the run before the first chair, naming the variable (conductor: no blind drain); tests/venue_dispatch/room_workspace_populated.test.ts now sets COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL to a fake drain service. ROUND 6d (on efd10a1): A2 — a drain key with no COLTRANE_DRAIN_URL makes NO claim; workOnce and `coltrane work` refuse at startup naming the variable (a post-claim refusal leases the row, spends an attempt, and cannot release it). ROUND 6e (on 0fdc905, review 5326586074): B1 the drain applies claim.budget_micro_usd (integer micro-dollars, #555) as the run's ceiling with the engine's batch-boundary rule — before each chair, settled spend < ceiling or the chair does not start; the in-flight chair is never interrupted and its settled cost counts; settled ≤ ceiling + one chair's actual cost; the stop is a named budget stop; no claim budget = no ceiling. B2 a `resumes` claim whose closed gig's status or outputs cannot be read (42501, error, no answer within 30 s) is refused by name, released non-terminally (the attempt refunds), nothing invoked — never a cold run. H6 unknown budget.* keys and a raw `resumes` argument are refused by name at the hosted door. ROUND 6f (on 7b554e6): B1c the budget gate runs before every dispatch batch inside a phase, not only at phase start; B1f the comparison is in integer micro-dollars (0.3×3 USD reaches a 900000 ceiling exactly; a float compare lets a fourth chair run). ROUND 6g (review 5327331488, on fe5ffb3 = main #559 merged): a `resumes` claim whose closed gig cannot be read — TRANSIENT (5xx, network, no answer) → refund + re-queue (B2); PERMANENT (42501 scope; an unseated/retired acting agent, 42501; outputs 42501; the closed gig gone) → the gig is terminated: failed, named reason, no refund, nothing invoked (U2); the queue advances past it (U3); a persistent transient failure still ends — the store refunds every non-terminal release (20260926040000) and the claim payload carries no attempts, so the engine must bound it itself (e.g. a failure count in its own gig's header manifest, readable through its own status) or the store must expose attempts/max_attempts on the claim (U4). B2's two 42501 cases (which asserted a refund) are retired. ROUND 7 (round-6 grade NOT MERGEABLE at 19a4812, non-author grader; the seat's two rulings). ROUND 6 WAS BEHAVIOURALLY WRONG AND ITS LAWS ASSERTED THE WRONGNESS AS CORRECT. Round 6 classified ANY answered 4xx on a resume-state read as PERMANENT and terminated the gig on poll 1 — failed, no refund, nothing invoked. On the live store as deployed TODAY that destroys every resuming gig: coltrane-ui #250 AS MERGED allows the OUTPUTS read of the gig a row resumes and REFUSES the STATUS read (403/42501); the widening to coltrane_mcp_gig_status is #253 and has NOT shipped. So the live sequence is outputs ok -> status 42501 -> 'permanent' -> terminated, and the other branch is fatal too (no seals -> the `nothing` branch -> terminated). tests/gig_runs_once_fixtures.ts documents it: the `resumedRead` DEFAULT models the world AFTER #253, while the live store today is the `refuse` case. Before round 6 these gigs were refunded and re-queued — they SPUN (the defect the review opened on) but they SURVIVED, and would have started working the moment the widening shipped. RULING R1 — THE FAIL-CLOSED DIRECTION WAS INVERTED, and it was the seat's error. 'Absent must mean DECLINE' is right only where the refusal is REVERSIBLE. Here it is not: terminating throws away the gig AND the money already spent on the closed gig's chairs, and no later poll undoes it, while the spin it replaces is recoverable by definition. A TRANSIENT FAILURE WHOSE BOUND CANNOT BE ESTABLISHED IS REFUNDED, NOT TERMINATED. The unbounded spin is still a real defect and is still bounded — never by trading a stall for destruction. RULING R2 — THE `nothing` BRANCH SPLITS. src/worker.ts:1420 is `const permanent = "nothing" in rebuilt || rebuilt.permanent;` — unconditional, never consulting whether the closed gig's status row EXISTS. The spec wrote case 4 as 'the closed gig NO LONGER EXISTS (no status row, no outputs)'; the code implemented 'sealed nothing'. Status row ABSENT -> permanent. Status row PRESENT with zero outputs -> COLD RUN (the justification 'a cold run re-pays for every chair the closed gig already sealed' collapses when zero chairs sealed; the cold run is then free and correct — and at a1d6925 it worked, invoked=['scan']). WHAT ROUND 7 SHIPS: LAWS AND A RED-SPEC ONLY — no production code; the classification change is the implementer's next round. New/re-pointed laws in tests/gig_runs_once_resume_unreadable.test.ts: U2 (the one permanent case, re-pointed to the ABSENT status row alone, plus the queue advancing); U3 (round 6's U4, kept); V1 a transient failure must be RETRIED — refunded and re-claimed — before it ends (the law round 6 lacked: U4 forbids the spin and never requires the retry, so instant termination leaves U4 GREEN — measured); V2a/V2b today's live-store 42501 on the status and the outputs read SURVIVES and RESUMES once the store widens; V3 one store hiccup fails BOTH reads (fetchDrainedGenomeHash(closed) and nextResumeReadFailureCount(own) are the SAME RPC on the SAME token and boundedWorkerRpc has no internal retry, so a 30-second store restart destroys every resuming gig claimed during it) — 5xx, ECONNRESET and timeout; V4 a 503 on the header CARRYING the bound is not a reason to destroy; V5 player mode with COLTRANE_DRAIN_KEY unset (remoteConfigured() false by construction, so the first transient failure is terminal every time, forever); V6 R2's cold run. S4 is CORRECTED, not merely noted: it passed over a gig that TERMINATED rather than ran, because the refusal's own header (drainRefusedResumeHeader) carries `resumes` unconditionally — the grader's plant P-A (cut the wire at src/worker.ts:1574) reds S4 at a1d6925 and PASSES at 19a4812 with all 4418 collected. `await closeO(store)` now closes the gig S4 resumes, and P-A reds it. COUNT HONESTY: round 6 credited 4 U2 + 2 U3 cases where 3 + 1 were falsifiable, because isPermanentStoreRefusal reads only e.status and never the message or code, so no src mutation can red `refuse` without `unseated`. Round 7 merges every collapsed pair into ONE law and keeps separate laws only where the src SITE differs (V2a the status read / V2b the outputs read; U2 the absent row / V6 the present row). SETTLED, do not re-investigate: coltrane-ui does NOT reject unknown manifest keys — `manifest` is an open jsonb column and the header upsert merges with `||` (baseline.sql:282), so manifest.resume_read_failures is accepted and stored in production.

IMPLEMENTER NOTE ON V4, and a residual the seat should rule on: R1 says an unestablishable bound is REFUNDED, which leaves a resume whose header can NEVER be written spinning without a worker-side bound. There is a second survival that is not a refund and not a destruction: hand the row back by NOT releasing it at all (status `abandoned`) and let the lease lapse — the store then re-queues it WITHOUT refunding the attempt, so the store's own max_attempts does the bounding and the gig survives up to the cap. V4 deliberately pins only the destruction (not failed, no terminal release, no gig_fail, and it resumes once the store recovers) so either survival satisfies it.

IMPLEMENTER NOTE ON V3: fetchDrainedGenomeHash and nextResumeReadFailureCount are the same RPC on the same token with no internal retry in boundedWorkerRpc. Even with the classification corrected, a single read is one round trip against a store that may be restarting; a retry inside boundedWorkerRpc would be a separate, cheaper fix than a re-claim, and is worth considering alongside it. V3 does not require it — it requires only that the gig is not destroyed.
